messages:
alex_w: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on mixed-precision routing when FP8 -> INT4 fallback triggers mid-sequence. Happens for long chat sessions where KV cache churn is high. Anyone else seen this?

maria_rm: yep saw similar in nightly perf job, reproduced locally on A100 nvlink stack. latency spikes + weird increased memcopy.

samir_k: can you paste the trace? sounds like kernel switch is forcing KV recompute instead of reusing cache.

alex_w: pasting trimmed profile from nvprof: 
```
TIMELINE: token 0-120 stable on fp8 kernel
Token 121 fallback -> int4 variant due to quant calibration drift
Event: KV_CACHE_INVALIDATE at token 121
Memcpy H2D: 12ms, KernelLaunch int4: 18ms, SerializeKV: 9ms
Overall per-token 47ms -> was 22ms before fallback
```

ida_ops: perf-ci-bot flagged this as a regression (regression_id: qmix-2026-03). CI job attached a stacktrace showing runtime picking int4 kernels because calibration_score dropped below threshold.

perf-ci-bot: Regression detected: qmix-2026-03. 95p latency before: 22ms, after fallback: 46ms. See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/qmix-2026-03

maria_rm: root cause seems twofold: 1) calibration check runs inline at sequence midpoint and is conservative, 2) kernel routing logic treats INT4 kernel as incompatible with existing KV layout so it rebuilds cache. Both combined cause double work.

samir_k: idea: expose two SDK knobs — (A) quantization.calibration_window = N tokens (how often we check), (B) quantization.routing_policy = [aggressive, conservative, sticky]. Default stays conservative. "sticky" would prefer keeping current kernel unless quality drops > X.

alex_w: love that. Also need a safety rail: quantization.safety_mode = [allow_fallback, lock_to_variant, degrade_gracefully]. If lock_to_variant, we never rebuild KV mid-sequence; instead we apply a soft-weighted-dequant to match outputs. That avoids KV rebuild cost but may have small quality drift.

jen_docs: for docs we should provide recommended presets: 
- preset: "latency-first" -> calibration_window=500, routing_policy=sticky, safety_mode=lock_to_variant
- preset: "quality-first" -> calibration_window=64, routing_policy=conservative, safety_mode=allow_fallback
- preset: "balanced" -> calibration_window=128, routing_policy=sticky, safety_mode=degrade_gracefully
Include example SDK snippets and tradeoffs.

ida_ops: need telemetry fields added: quant.preset_used, quant.calibration_score, quant.kv_rebuild_count, quant.fallback_reason. We'll add these to tracing so console can plot regressions.

maria_rm: small implementation note: sticky routing requires kernel compatibility table that tells whether KV-layouts are interchangeable between variants. For some int4 kernels layout differs, so we must ensure a fallback path that marks them incompatible.

samir_k: agreed. We'll add KernelDescriptor.compatible_with list and a cheap checksum of KV-layout to decide. If incompatible, fallback to rebuild but we can add incremental copy optimization to avoid full serialize.

alex_w: for SDK naming suggestions: keep short, dot-namespaced: quant.preset, quant.window_tokens, quant.routing, quant.safety. We should also expose a readonly field quant.effective_variant in responses so users know which kernel served which token.

jen_docs: draft doc blurb: 
"Quantization knobs let you control how the runtime balances throughput and model quality when using mixed precision kernels. Use presets for typical workloads; use window/routing knobs to tune long-session chatbots where KV reuse is important. Safety modes control whether the runtime will rebuild KV mid-sequence, lock a variant for the whole sequence, or apply graceful degradation."

ida_ops: I'm worried about users accidentally setting window too large and never re-calibrating; we should add console warnings when quant.calibration_age > X and quant.preset=latency-first.

maria_rm: also add a canary rule in rollout: when changing default preset, gradually ramp per-customer and monitor quant.kv_rebuild_count and 95p latency.

samir_k: next steps: I'll prototype sticky routing + compat table. ida_ops will add telemetry and warning hooks. jen_docs will write SDK examples + three presets. alex_w will run a targeted perf matrix across sequence lengths [32,128,512] and generate plots.

alex_w: thanks all — ping me on updates. I pushed a small repro to /tmp/qmix-repro and referenced in the CI run. @jen_docs please include a short note in docs about potential edge-case where lock_to_variant may reduce output fidelity slightly. :thumbsup:

jen_docs: will do. I'll open a docs PR by EOD and link here.

perf-ci-bot: Job qmix-2026-03 re-run queued by alex_w.
